svg.title: How Pi-hole blocks ads for every device
svg.desc: 1: the router's DHCP tells each device that its DNS server is 192.168.1.2, the Pi-hole. 2: the device asks Pi-hole for every name it looks up. 3: if the name is on a blocklist, such as doubleclick.net, Pi-hole answers 0.0.0.0 and the ad never loads; if not, such as raspberrypi.com, Pi-hole asks an upstream DNS server (Cloudflare or Quad9) and passes the real address back, so the page loads. Warning: a secondary DNS such as 8.8.8.8 lets devices skip Pi-hole.

g.text: Don’t set a secondary DNS like 8.8.8.8:
devices use it at random and skip the blocking
